explainBack.question: Why does installing the Gemini Windows app not mean Gemini can now see your screen, files or email?
explainBack.answer: Because the app only changes the route into the same online service: Alt + Space opens a window beside your work, but Gemini receives only what you deliberately give it — a pasted draft, an uploaded image, or a Google app such as Gmail or Drive that you explicitly choose to connect. On a work or school account, even having the app depends on an administrator enabling Gemini, so installation alone grants neither capability nor data access.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: An accurate answer must distinguish the entry route from the service's capabilities (P004), cite the explicit choice to upload or connect apps (P006), note admin control on managed accounts (P005), and reject the automatic-visibility inference (P008).
explainBack.assessment: The article fully supports this answer: P004 supplies the route-versus-capability model, P005 the admin condition, P006 the explicit-connection mechanism, and P008 directly names and rejects the automatic-access assumption. The explain-back succeeds in ordinary language.

unseenTransfer.scenario: A colleague hears that a different AI vendor has released a macOS menu-bar assistant with a global hotkey, and worries that once IT installs it, the assistant will automatically read her calendar and inbox to 'be helpful'. Her company uses managed Apple IDs and a managed identity provider.
unseenTransfer.question: Should she assume the new desktop app can read her calendar and inbox, and what should she check before using it?
unseenTransfer.answer: No. Applying the article's mechanism: a desktop app is a new door into the same service, not a new capability. The assistant will only reach her calendar or inbox if she (or an admin policy) explicitly connects those services, and on a managed account her administrator controls whether the app and its connections are enabled at all. She should check which account the app signs into, read the connection/permission screens before granting anything, and confirm with IT what the admin policy already enables.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: A correct transfer must reuse route-versus-capability (P004/P009), the explicit-connection condition (P006), and administrator control on managed accounts (P005), rather than facts specific to Gemini or Windows.
unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's mechanism transfers cleanly: nothing in the answer depends on Gemini-specific details, only on the general model of entry routes, explicit connections and admin-gated managed accounts that the article establishes. Transfer succeeds.

learningDisposition.rationale: All reader outcomes and news checks pass and all failure families are clear; explain-back and the invented transfer scenario both succeed on the article's stated mechanism, so no reusable defect is observed.
